```{r}
# ===== Stimulus validation using IDs directly from dat$Stimulus =====
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lme4)

# 0) Safety + factor coding
stopifnot(all(c("Participant","Stimulus","aesthetic","emotional_expressive","Confidence_label") %in% names(dat)))

dat <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(Stimulus), !is.na(Participant)) %>%
  mutate(
    Stimulus    = factor(Stimulus),
    Participant = factor(Participant)
  )

# How many unique stimuli?
all_stims <- levels(dat$Stimulus)
length(all_stims)

# 1) Stimulus-level descriptives (via participant means first)
#    This avoids overweighting participants with more trials on a clip.
stim_desc <- dat %>%
  group_by(Stimulus, Participant) %>%
  summarise(
    m_aesthetic  = mean(aesthetic, na.rm = TRUE),
    m_emotion    = mean(emotional_expressive, na.rm = TRUE),
    m_confidence = mean(Confidence_label, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Stimulus) %>%
  summarise(
    n_participants  = n(),                                # number of participants who rated this stimulus
    mean_aesthetic  = mean(m_aesthetic,  na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_aesthetic    = sd(m_aesthetic,    na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_emotion    = mean(m_emotion,    na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_emotion      = sd(m_emotion,      na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_confidence = mean(m_confidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_confidence   = sd(m_confidence,   na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Stimulus)

# Quick checks
nrow(stim_desc)                # should equal number of unique stimuli present in dat
summary(stim_desc$n_participants)

# 2) ICCs (stimulus-level reliability) via mixed models
#    ICC_stim = Var(Stimulus) / [Var(Stimulus) + Var(Residual)]
icc_from_model <- function(formula, data) {
  m <- lmer(formula,
            data = data,
            REML = TRUE,
            control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e6)))
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))
  var_stim <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Stimulus"]
  var_res  <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"]
  icc_stim <- var_stim / (var_stim + var_res)
  list(model = m, icc_stim = icc_stim)
}

icc_aesthetic <- icc_from_model(aesthetic ~ 1 + (1|Stimulus) + (1|Participant), dat)
icc_emotion   <- icc_from_model(emotional_expressive ~ 1 + (1|Stimulus) + (1|Participant), dat)
icc_conf      <- icc_from_model(Confidence_label ~ 1 + (1|Stimulus) + (1|Participant), dat)

cat("\n--- Stimulus ICCs (proportion of variance at stimulus level) ---\n")
cat(sprintf("Aesthetic:            ICC_stim = %.3f\n", icc_aesthetic$icc_stim))
cat(sprintf("Emotional/Expressive: ICC_stim = %.3f\n", icc_emotion$icc_stim))
cat(sprintf("Confidence (Task 2):  ICC_stim = %.3f\n", icc_conf$icc_stim))

# 3) Outlier detection at stimulus level (> 2 SD from stimulus mean distribution on any metric)
zflag <- function(x) (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)

stim_outliers <- stim_desc %>%
  mutate(
    z_aesthetic = zflag(mean_aesthetic),
    z_emotion   = zflag(mean_emotion),
    z_conf      = zflag(mean_confidence),
    outlier_any = abs(z_aesthetic) > 2 | abs(z_emotion) > 2 | abs(z_conf) > 2
  ) %>%
  filter(outlier_any) %>%
  arrange(Stimulus)

cat("\n--- Potential stimulus outliers (>2 SD on any metric) ---\n")
print(stim_outliers %>% select(Stimulus, starts_with("mean_"), starts_with("z_")))

# 4) Stimulus-level correlations (means across stimuli)
cor_mat <- stim_desc %>%
  select(mean_aesthetic, mean_emotion, mean_confidence) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cat("\n--- Stimulus-level correlations (means across stimuli) ---\n")
print(round(cor_mat, 3))

```

```{r}
# aesthetic H1(a)

# Libraries
library(dplyr)
library(psych)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)    # adds p-values to lmer
library(emmeans)     # EMMs & contrasts
library(performance) # R2 etc.
library(conflicted)

# Resolve function-name conflicts for this session
conflicts_prefer(psych::alpha)   # alpha() = reliability
conflicts_prefer(lmerTest::lmer) # lmer() = lmerTest version

# --- Make items numeric (safe if they came in as factors/character) ---
data_task <- data_task %>%
  mutate(
    enjoyable = as.numeric(as.character(Enjoyable)),
    likeable  = as.numeric(as.character(Likeable)),
    pleasing  = as.numeric(as.character(Pleasing))
  )

# --- Reliability (Cronbach's alpha) ---
alpha_res <- psych::alpha(data_task[, c("enjoyable", "likeable", "pleasing")])
alpha_res  # prints full table
# If you want the number inline:
# alpha_res$total$raw_alpha

# --- Composite score ---
data_task <- data_task %>%
  mutate(aesthetic = rowMeans(dplyr::select(., enjoyable, likeable, pleasing), na.rm = TRUE))

# --- Prep analysis data ---
dat <- data_task %>%
  filter(!is.na(aesthetic), !is.na(Condition), !is.na(Participant), !is.na(Stimulus)) %>%
  mutate(
    Condition   = factor(Condition, levels = c("AI", "Human")), # AI = reference
    Participant = factor(Participant),
    Stimulus    = factor(Stimulus)
  )

# --- Mixed model (random intercepts for Participant & Stimulus) ---
m1 <- lmer(aesthetic ~ Condition + (1 | Participant) + (1 | Stimulus),
           data = dat, REML = FALSE)
summary(m1)

# --- Enable Satterthwaite df in emmeans for large N ---
emmeans::emm_options(
  pbkrtest.limit = nrow(dat),
  lmerTest.limit = nrow(dat),
  lmer.df        = "satterthwaite"  # be explicit
)

# --- Estimated marginal means and contrast (Human - AI) with Satterthwaite df ---
emm <- emmeans(m1, ~ Condition)
emm
contrast(emm, "revpairwise") %>% summary(infer = TRUE)

# --- (Optional) R2 for reporting ---
performance::r2(m1)

# --- (Optional) Random slopes by Participant; compare to m1 ---
m2 <- try(lmer(aesthetic ~ Condition + (1 + Condition | Participant) + (1 | Stimulus),
               data = dat, REML = FALSE))
if (!inherits(m2, "try-error")) {
  print(anova(m1, m2))  # chi-square test of fit improvement
  # If you decide to report m2 instead, you can get EMMs the same way:
  # emm2 <- emmeans(m2, ~ Condition)
  # contrast(emm2, "revpairwise") %>% summary(infer = TRUE)
}
# (You already fit m1 earlier)
# Ensure emmeans uses Satterthwaite df for large N
emmeans::emm_options(
  pbkrtest.limit = nrow(dat),
  lmerTest.limit = nrow(dat),
  lmer.df        = "satterthwaite"
)

# Estimated marginal means and contrast (now with df, not Inf)
emm <- emmeans::emmeans(m1, ~ Condition)
emm
emmeans::contrast(emm, "revpairwise") %>% summary(infer = TRUE)


# --- (Optional) Diagnostics ---
# check_model(m1)  # opens plots

```

```{r}
#emotional_expressive H1(b)

# Libraries
library(dplyr)
library(psych)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)    # adds p-values to lmer
library(emmeans)     # EMMs & contrasts
library(performance) # R2 etc.
library(conflicted)

# Resolve function-name conflicts for this session
suppressMessages({
  conflicts_prefer(psych::alpha)   # alpha() = reliability
  conflicts_prefer(lmerTest::lmer) # lmer() = lmerTest version
})

# --- Make items numeric (safe if factors/characters) ---
data_task <- data_task %>%
  mutate(
    emotional  = as.numeric(as.character(Emotional)),
    expressive = as.numeric(as.character(Expressive))
  )

# --- Reliability (Cronbach's alpha) ---
alpha_res_b <- psych::alpha(data_task[, c("emotional", "expressive")])
alpha_res_b  # prints full table
# alpha_res_b$total$raw_alpha  # if you want the value for reporting

# --- Composite score ---
data_task <- data_task %>%
  mutate(emotional_expressive = rowMeans(dplyr::select(., emotional, expressive), na.rm = TRUE))

# --- Prep analysis data ---
dat <- data_task %>%
  filter(!is.na(emotional_expressive), !is.na(Condition), !is.na(Participant), !is.na(Stimulus)) %>%
  mutate(
    Condition   = factor(Condition, levels = c("AI", "Human")), # AI = reference
    Participant = factor(Participant),
    Stimulus    = factor(Stimulus)
  )

# --- Mixed model (random intercepts for Participant & Stimulus) ---
m1 <- lmer(emotional_expressive ~ Condition + (1 | Participant) + (1 | Stimulus),
           data = dat, REML = FALSE)
summary(m1)

# --- Enable Satterthwaite df in emmeans for large N ---
emmeans::emm_options(
  pbkrtest.limit = nrow(dat),
  lmerTest.limit = nrow(dat),
  lmer.df        = "satterthwaite"
)

# --- Estimated marginal means and contrast (Human - AI) with Satterthwaite df ---
emm_b <- emmeans(m1, ~ Condition)
emm_b
contrast(emm_b, "revpairwise") %>% summary(infer = TRUE)

# --- (Optional) R2 for reporting ---
performance::r2(m1)

# --- (Optional) Random slopes by Participant; compare to m1 ---
m2 <- try(lmer(emotional_expressive ~ Condition + (1 + Condition | Participant) + (1 | Stimulus),
               data = dat, REML = FALSE))
if (!inherits(m2, "try-error")) {
  print(anova(m1, m2))  # chi-square test of fit improvement
  # If you decide to report m2 instead:
  # emm_b2 <- emmeans(m2, ~ Condition)
  # contrast(emm_b2, "revpairwise") %>% summary(infer = TRUE)
}

# --- (Optional) Diagnostics ---
# check_model(m1)  # opens plots
```

```{r}
#checking if top 25% emotional_expressive stims have different results
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)

# 1. Create the composite score
data_task <- data_task %>%
  mutate(
    emotional_expressive = rowMeans(select(., Emotional, Expressive), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# 2. Get average score per stimulus
stimulus_emotions <- data_task %>%
  group_by(Stimulus) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_emotion_expr = mean(emotional_expressive, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3. Find stimuli with mean score >= 4
high_emotion_stimuli <- stimulus_emotions %>%
  filter(mean_emotion_expr >= 4) %>%
  pull(Stimulus)

# 4. Filter main data to just these stimuli
high_data <- data_task %>%
  filter(Stimulus %in% high_emotion_stimuli)

# 5. Fit mixed model on subset
m_high <- lmer(emotional_expressive ~ Condition + (1|Participant) + (1|Stimulus),
               data = high_data, REML = FALSE)

# Model summary
summary(m_high)

# 6. Estimated marginal means
emm_high <- emmeans(m_high, ~ Condition)
print(emm_high)

# 7. Difference with 95% CI
contrast(emm_high, method = "revpairwise") %>% summary(infer = TRUE)

```

```{r}
#H2(a) Media Professionalism as moderator

library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)

# Make sure IDs are same type
data_task <- data_task %>% mutate(Participant = as.character(Participant))
data_ppt   <- data_ppt   %>% mutate(Participant = as.character(Participant))

# Merge TRUE/FALSE variable
dat <- data_task %>%
  left_join(
    data_ppt %>% select(Participant, media_professional),
    by = "Participant"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    media_professional = ifelse(media_professional == TRUE, "Yes", "No"),
    media_professional = factor(media_professional, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
    Condition = factor(Condition, levels = c("AI", "Human")),
    Participant = factor(Participant),
    Stimulus = factor(Stimulus)
  )

# Function to run model
run_interaction_model <- function(dv) {
  message("=== Results for ", dv, " ===")
  form <- as.formula(paste(dv, "~ Condition * media_professional + (1|Participant) + (1|Stimulus)"))
  m <- lmer(form, data = dat, REML = FALSE)
  print(summary(m))
  
  emm <- emmeans(m, ~ Condition | media_professional)
  print(emm)
  print(contrast(emm, method = "revpairwise"))
}

# Run for aesthetic
run_interaction_model("aesthetic")

# Run for emotional_expressive
run_interaction_model("emotional_expressive")



```

```{r}
# Identify unusually long completion times

# Calculate median and IQR
median_time <- median(data_ppt$Experiment_Duration, na.rm = TRUE)
iqr_time <- IQR(data_ppt$Experiment_Duration, na.rm = TRUE)

# Set threshold (here: more than 3×IQR above the median)
upper_threshold <- median_time + 3 * iqr_time

# Flag participants above threshold
data_ppt$long_time_flag <- data_ppt$Experiment_Duration > upper_threshold

# View flagged participants
long_takers <- data_ppt %>% 
  filter(long_time_flag == TRUE)

# Convert to minutes
data_ppt$time_elapsed_min <- data_ppt$Experiment_Duration / 60000

# Check summary
summary(data_ppt$Experiment_Duration_min)

# Print flagged participants
print(long_takers)

# Summary count of who is flagged
table(data_ppt$long_time_flag)

# Check threshold value for reference
upper_threshold

```

```{r}
#H3 if media people were overall more confident
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)

# Ensure IDs match type
data_task <- data_task %>% mutate(Participant = as.character(Participant))
data_ppt  <- data_ppt  %>% mutate(Participant = as.character(Participant))

# Merge media_professional into main dataset & create absolute confidence variable
dat <- data_task %>%
  left_join(
    data_ppt %>% select(Participant, media_professional),
    by = "Participant"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    media_professional = ifelse(media_professional == TRUE, "Yes", "No"),
    media_professional = factor(media_professional, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
    Condition = factor(Condition, levels = c("AI", "Human")),
    Participant = factor(Participant),
    Stimulus = factor(Stimulus),
    confidence_abs = abs(Confidence_label - 3)  # distance from midpoint (0-3 scale)
  )

# Mixed model: Confidence by Condition and Media Professional status
m_conf <- lmer(confidence_abs ~ Condition * media_professional + 
                 (1|Participant) + (1|Stimulus),
               data = dat, REML = FALSE)

# Model summary
summary(m_conf)

# Estimated marginal means for each group/condition
emm <- emmeans(m_conf, ~ Condition | media_professional)
print(emm)

# Label effect within each group
contrast(emm, method = "revpairwise")

```

```{r}
#H4(a) Labelling influences task two confidence

library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)

# Ensure coding is correct: AI as reference, Human as the contrast
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Condition   = factor(Condition, levels = c("AI","Human")),
    Participant = factor(Participant),
    Stimulus    = factor(Stimulus)
  )

# H4(a): Does the Task 1 label (Condition) influence Task 2 ratings?
m_h4 <- lmer(Confidence_label ~ Condition + (1|Participant) + (1|Stimulus),
             data = dat, REML = FALSE)

summary(m_h4)

# Estimated marginal means and the Human–AI difference
emm <- emmeans(m_h4, ~ Condition)
emm
contrast(emm, method = "revpairwise") %>% summary(infer = TRUE)


```

```{r}
#Alternate visual
# ---- Diverging (horizontal) directional confidence plot ----
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Center Task-2 ratings at 0 = "unsure" (so -3..+3)
dat2 <- dat %>%
  mutate(conf_centered = Confidence_label - 3)  # -3 = certain AI, +3 = certain Human

# Participant-level means (avoid trial-count imbalance)
dat_pp <- dat2 %>%
  group_by(Participant, Condition) %>%
  summarise(conf_centered = mean(conf_centered, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Group summaries (means + 95% CI)
sum_pp <- dat_pp %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    mean = mean(conf_centered, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd   = sd(conf_centered, na.rm = TRUE),
    se   = sd / sqrt(n),
    lo   = mean - 1.96 * se,
    hi   = mean + 1.96 * se,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Okabe–Ito palette
pal <- c(AI = "#0072B2", Human = "#D55E00")

# Pretty labels for the centered x-axis
brks <- -3:3
labs <- c("−3\ncertain AI","−2","−1","0\nunsure","+1","+2","+3\ncertain Human")

ggplot() +
  # Violin on raw trials for shape (horizontal)
  geom_violin(
    data = dat2,
    aes(y = Condition, x = conf_centered, fill = Condition),
    trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.35, color = NA
  ) +
  # Participant-level dots (means), jittered for visibility
  geom_jitter(
    data = dat_pp,
    aes(y = Condition, x = conf_centered, color = Condition),
    height = 0.12, width = 0, alpha = 0.5, size = 1.6
  ) +
  # Mean ± 95% CI (bold, black)
  geom_point(
    data = sum_pp,
    aes(y = Condition, x = mean),
    color = "black", size = 3
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    data = sum_pp,
    aes(y = Condition, xmin = lo, xmax = hi),
    height = 0.12, color = "black", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  # Reference line at 0 = "unsure"
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey55") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-3, 3), breaks = brks, labels = labs, expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(
    title = "Directional influence of Task-1 label on Task-2 ratings (diverging scale)",
    subtitle = "Centered at 0 = unsure (− = AI direction, + = Human direction)",
    x = "Task-2 rating relative to ‘unsure’",
    y = "Initial Task-1 label"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Keep all valid data in original scale (0 = certain AI, 3 = unsure, 6 = certain Human)
dat2 <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(Confidence_label))

# Summarise means and CIs
summary_data <- dat2 %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rating = mean(Confidence_label, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(Confidence_label, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    lower = mean_rating - 1.96 * se,
    upper = mean_rating + 1.96 * se,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot
ggplot(dat2, aes(x = Condition, y = Confidence_label, fill = Condition)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.4, color = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = summary_data, aes(x = Condition, y = mean_rating), 
             color = "black", size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_errorbar(data = summary_data, aes(x = Condition, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                width = 0.1, color = "black", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  # Add dashed lines for AI, Unsure, Human
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 6, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.1, y = 0.2, label = "Certain AI", hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.1, y = 3.2, label = "Unsure", hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.1, y = 6.2, label = "Certain Human", hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#619CFF", "#F8766D")) +
  labs(
    x = "Initial Task 1 Label",
    y = "Task 2 Confidence Rating",
    title = "Directional Influence of Task 1 Labels on Task 2 Ratings"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 6)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

```{r}
#emotional_expressive equals more human?
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)

# Prepare dataset
dat_int <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    emo_c = scale(emotional_expressive, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE),
    Condition = factor(Condition, levels = c("AI", "Human")),
    Participant = factor(Participant),
    Stimulus = factor(Stimulus)
  )

# Main effects model
m_main_emo <- lmer(
  Confidence_label ~ emo_c + Condition + (1 | Participant) + (1 | Stimulus),
  data = dat_int,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Interaction model
m_int_emo <- lmer(
  Confidence_label ~ emo_c * Condition + (1 | Participant) + (1 | Stimulus),
  data = dat_int,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Compare models
anova(m_main_emo, m_int_emo)

# Summary of interaction model
summary(m_int_emo)

# Simple slopes with emmeans
library(emmeans)
emtrends(m_int_emo, ~ Condition, var = "emo_c")
contrast(emtrends(m_int_emo, ~ Condition, var = "emo_c"), "pairwise")

```

```{r}
#visual rep 
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Create prediction data from your fitted model
pred_data <- ggeffects::ggpredict(m_int_emo, terms = c("emo_c [all]", "Condition"))

# Plot
ggplot(pred_data, aes(x = x, y = predicted, color = group)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high, fill = group), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  labs(
    x = "Emotionality Rating (centered)",
    y = "Predicted Task 2 Confidence Rating",
    color = "Initial Label",
    fill = "Initial Label",
    title = "Interaction Between Emotionality and Initial Label on Task 2 Confidence"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#619CFF", "#F8766D")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#619CFF", "#F8766D")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

```{r}
#Aesthetic higher confidence human?
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)

# 0) Prep (reuse your data frame 'dat')
dat_int <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    aesthetic_c = scale(aesthetic, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE),
    Condition   = factor(Condition, levels = c("AI","Human")),
    Participant = factor(Participant),
    Stimulus    = factor(Stimulus)
  )

# 1) Fit models: without vs with interaction
m_main <- lmer(
  Confidence_label ~ aesthetic_c + Condition + (1|Participant) + (1|Stimulus),
  data = dat_int, REML = FALSE
)

m_int <- lmer(
  Confidence_label ~ aesthetic_c * Condition + (1|Participant) + (1|Stimulus),
  data = dat_int, REML = FALSE
)

# 2) Compare models (does slope differ by Condition?)
anova(m_main, m_int)  # significant p => interaction present

summary(m_int)        # coefficients, including the interaction term

# 3) Simple slopes (AI vs Human): slope of aesthetic_c within each Condition
slopes <- emtrends(m_int, specs = "Condition", var = "aesthetic_c")
slopes                     # shows slope (estimate), SE, df, t, p for AI and Human
contrast(slopes, "pairwise")  # tests if the two slopes differ from each other

# 4) Build prediction grid for plotting
#    (predicted Task-2 rating across a range of aesthetic values, by Condition)
a_range <- with(dat_int, seq(min(aesthetic_c, na.rm=TRUE),
                             max(aesthetic_c, na.rm=TRUE), length.out = 100))
pred_df <- emmeans(m_int, ~ aesthetic_c | Condition,
                   at = list(aesthetic_c = a_range)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(pred = emmean, lower = lower.CL, upper = upper.CL)

head(pred_df)  # ready for ggplot: aes(x = aesthetic_c, y = pred, color = Condition)

```

```{r}
#visual
library(ggeffects)
library(ggplot2)

# Prepare dataset
dat_int <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    aesthetic_c = scale(aesthetic, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE),
    Condition = factor(Condition, levels = c("AI", "Human")),
    Participant = factor(Participant),
    Stimulus = factor(Stimulus)
  )

# Fit interaction model
m_int_aesthetic <- lmer(
  Confidence_label ~ aesthetic_c * Condition + (1 | Participant) + (1 | Stimulus),
  data = dat_int,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Get predictions for plotting
preds_aesthetic <- ggpredict(m_int_aesthetic, terms = c("aesthetic_c", "Condition"))

# Plot
ggplot(preds_aesthetic, aes(x = x, y = predicted, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high, fill = group), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#619CFF", "#F8766D")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#619CFF", "#F8766D")) +
  labs(
    x = "Aesthetic Rating (centered)",
    y = "Predicted Task 2 Confidence Rating",
    colour = "Initial Task 1 Label",
    fill = "Initial Task 1 Label",
    title = "Interaction: Aesthetic Rating × Initial Label"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```
